results:
The search confirms that mathlib began in 2017 but did not turn up the initial commit itself or its exact date.

- **Origins in 2017:** A 2019 paper by the mathlib community says in the summer of 2017, much of the core library for Lean was factored out of the system repository. This code became the base for mathlib. A 2020 paper by the same community credits Mario Carneiro and Johannes Hölzl at Carnegie Mellon University with initially leading the project.
- **Exact start month:** A lecture file by Floris van Doorn (2019) says the library was started in July 2017 to separate the mathematics library from the core library. This is the only source I found giving a month, so treat it as secondary.
- **Lean 3 context:** The Lean 3.0 series first shipped on January 20, 2017, so mathlib was created shortly after that release. The Lean reference notes that development of Lean 4 began in 2018.
- **Growth and Lean 4 port:** A University of Bonn seminar slide lists 2017 Mathlib was created, and mathlib was successfully ported to Lean 4 in 2023 through a community effort.

I did not find a source for the literal first commit or its hash. An aggregator wiki (aiwiki.ai) also says the project begun in 2017 as a separate repository, but it is not an authoritative source. The GitHub history of leanprover-community/mathlib (or mathlib3) would be the place to confirm the first commit date.

content.text:
**答案:2017 年。**

依据:
- 2019 年 mathlib 社区的论文《The Lean mathematical library》说,2017 年夏天,Lean 核心库中的大部分内容被拆分出来,成为 mathlib 的基础。
- Floris van Doorn 2019 年的讲座文件称,mathlib 始于 2017 年 7 月,目的是把数学库从核心库中分离出来。这是我找到的唯一给出月份的来源,可信度较低。
- 波恩大学的 Mathlib 研讨课幻灯片也把"Mathlib created"列在 2017 年。

我没有查到最初那次提交的确切日期。想确认的话,可以看 leanprover-community/mathlib(mathlib3)仓库的提交历史。

Sources:
- [The Lean mathematical library (arXiv 1910.09336)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.09336)
- [lecture-mathlib.lean (Floris van Doorn)](https://github.com/jesse-michael-han/hanoi-lean-2019/blob/master/src/floris/lecture-mathlib.lean)
- [Bonn Seminar Mathlib 幻灯片](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/rothgang/slides_BonnSeminarMathlib.pdf)
